title: Watch a log file live and alert when a pattern appears
summary: Follow a log while new lines are added and print a message whenever a line matches a word or pattern, such as ERROR. Only new lines are checked. Stop the watch with Ctrl+C.

aliases.text: follow log and react to match
следить за логом и сообщать об ошибке
оповещение когда в логе появляется слово

steps.explain: Find the log file and check that it is the one the program writes to. Its size should grow while the program runs.
steps.expect: A line with the file size, the owner and the last change time.

placeholders.name: LOG_FILE
placeholders.description: Log file that the program writes to

steps.explain: Check that the pattern matches lines already in the file. A count of 0 means nothing matches yet, so check the spelling and capital letters.

placeholders.name: PATTERN
placeholders.description: Word or pattern to alert on (extended regular expression)

placeholders.name: LOG_FILE
placeholders.description: Log file that the program writes to

steps.explain: Start the watch. tail -n 0 starts at the end, so only new lines are checked. -F keeps following the file after it is rotated. grep --line-buffered passes each match on at once. Each match prints an ALERT line with the time.
steps.cmd: tail -n 0 -F <LOG_FILE> | grep --line-buffered -E '<PATTERN>' | while IFS= read -r line; do echo "ALERT $(date +%T) $line"; done
steps.expect: An ALERT line each time the program writes a matching line.

placeholders.name: LOG_FILE

alternatives.explain: Show each match as a desktop notification instead of a terminal line. Needs the notify-send command (package libnotify).
alternatives.cmd: tail -n 0 -F <LOG_FILE> | grep --line-buffered -E '<PATTERN>' | while IFS= read -r line; do notify-send "Log alert" "$line"; done

placeholders.name: LOG_FILE
placeholders.description: Log file that the program writes to

placeholders.name: PATTERN
placeholders.description: Word or pattern to alert on (extended regular expression)

steps.explain: Stop the watch with Ctrl+C in the same terminal. The log is only read, never changed.

warnings: Only lines written after the watch started are reported. Earlier errors are not shown; step 2 counts them.
